our_argument_summary: The dome's refraction fix (calling the apparent 5,733 km sun altitude an n(r) optical illusion) commits the physical sun to an altitude bounded by H(r) at the sun's seasonal orbital radius. Because H(r) is monotonic and the sun's radius swings between the Tropic of Cancer (June, r=7,400) and Tropic of Capricorn (December, r=12,614), the physical-altitude cap swings from ~3,618 km (June) down to ~1,975 km (December) — an 83% swing — while the apparent altitude is held fixed. n(r) has no time dependence, so it cannot deliver two different refractive lifts at the same radius; the section argues this cascades into tidal (WIN-046), solar-elevation (WIN-056), firmament-scaling (WIN-044) and Schumann (WIN-002/-029) WINs.

This is the same internal-arithmetic-inconsistency class as the original c1 hole 0, in the same section whose explicit rhetorical anchor is 'nothing here is contested arithmetic' — which invites precisely this kind of subtraction audit. The patch that was meant to resolve the inconsistency half-resolved it and left a self-auditable 3-km error one paragraph below.

deeper_analysis: This is a verification-class re-review of queue_id 476 (section-rewrite). Method: recompute every number in the seasonal-indeterminacy H3 from the dome's published H(r) and 5,733 km apparent altitude, then diff against the c1 holes to confirm each was patched. Result: 4 of the c1 holes (0,1,2,3) are correctly patched; the optional hole 4 remains open. The single new finding is a propagation gap: correcting the December bound 1,978->1,975 should have rippled to the only other place that number is consumed — the December refractive-lift figure (5,733 minus the bound). It did not, leaving '3,755' (=5,733-1,978) where '3,758' (=5,733-1,975) belongs. Counter-argument considered: the discrepancy is 3 km / 0.08%, both the 83% swing and 78% refraction ratios round identically under old and new bounds, and the figure sits in a parenthetical, so a generous reader would never notice. That is true on magnitude — which is why current_verdict_holds and the action is minor_edit, not major_rewrite. But the c1 reviewer rated the identical 3-km class of error 'moderate' precisely because the section advertises exact arithmetic; keeping the severity consistent, this is moderate. Net: the patch landed but is one one-character edit short of clean.

advocate_mode.strongest_dome_defense: A dome defender cannot use the 3,755/3,758 slip to rescue the model — it is an error in OUR favor's arithmetic, not the dome's. The defender's only live move against the section as a whole remains: post a seasonal-amplitude curve for the apparent altitude (as Earth's axial tilt does), which would convert the 'suspiciously fixed 5,733 km' into a modeled seasonal track. The section pre-empts this in the EXP's anticipated_objections; the dome has not published such a curve (raw-text/05-model.txt line 38). The defender would also note that 'physical sun must sit below H(r)' assumes the sun sits at its current orbital radius's ceiling rather than below it — but the section's range argument holds for any sun at-or-below the cap, so this does not help.
advocate_mode.does_it_survive: No. The defender's best move is unaddressed-but-acknowledged, not a refutation.
